executiveSummary: GM0222's generated 2025 code, Doetinchem name, Gelderland province, Noord- en Oost-Gelderland safety-region assignment, 60,049-person control total, 84 neighbourhoods, three BAG places and twelve settlement labels are coherent. All ten canonical exercises execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply; exact-zero input, finite bounds, reconciliation, monotone attributable burden, causal-ledger closure, standing-water recovery guards and layer invariance pass. Release remains correction-required. Pluvial, river, coastal, heat and wildfire use the exact same complete 84-neighbourhood order although Doetinchem and Waterschap Rijn en IJssel publish distinct rainfall, road-passability, heat, groundwater and flood layers. A controlled wildfire source inside the official Slangenburg mixed-forest polygon ranks its containing neighbourhood only 28th. The river preset holds normalized inundation stress at 2.000988 through T+72, reporting 28,725 affected people-equivalent, 2,128,326.509 attributable person-hours and only 15.247% supply availability without a selected Oude IJssel/IJssel boundary, defence state, breach, connected footprint, arrival or recession. All lifelines reuse the same ten NWB road links; 59 public water objects, rail/transit, Slingeland Hospital, current absence of emergency support points and public power/provider context do not supply physical topology, live capacity, backup or restoration. Public-data integrations are available, but unavailable or security-sensitive infrastructure must remain Unknown or transparently synthetic.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The fresh official GM0222 row gives Doetinchem, 60,049 residents, density 760 per square kilometre, 13,688 residents aged 65+ and 9,860 one-person households.

The 84 generated neighbourhood source rows sum to 60,050 residents, one above the municipality control (+0.002%), 27,100 households and 13,650 residents aged 65+; published small-area values are not silently overwritten.

The OData service is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0. CBS labels the 2025 table as receiving quarterly additions; randomized rounding, suppression and incomplete variables remain source semantics, not zero.

Simulation role is official demographic/context and allocation denominator only. Registered residence is not incident-time presence at schools, workplaces, stations, care sites, roads or hazard footprints.

evidenceSources.title: CBS Gebiedsindelingen 2025 non-generalized geometry and national settlement/transport reference APIs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary; current generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS reference editions
supports: Fresh full-resolution GM0222 geometry has one MultiPolygon component, one ring and 4,110 positions with bbox [6.144688334128284, 51.92278202342862, 6.416081865598491, 51.99426071114093]. The generated overview has the same one-component/one-ring topology but only 174 positions and contains centre [6.280163177126242, 51.965125985136545].
The bundle has eleven districts, 84 neighbourhoods and BAG places Doetinchem, Gaanderen and Wehl. BRT supplies twelve labels: five buurtschappen, one deelkern and six woonkernen.

Ten logical border links use A18, N315, N316, N317, N813, N814 and N815 toward Montferland, Oude IJsselstreek and Bronckhorst. Doetinchem, Gaanderen, Doetinchem De Huet and Wehl are ProRail stations; the bundle has 77 GTFS stop areas.

CBS boundary OGC is half-yearly/CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark; BRT is CC BY 4.0; NWB OGC/download is monthly/CC0 1.0; ProRail reference geometry is manually refreshed/CC0 1.0. The generated OVapi GTFS feed is best effort/free-use with no SLA. These are reference data, not incident-time passability or utility topology.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatadaptatiestrategie Doetinchem and municipal crisis-preparedness information
evidenceSources.edition: Strategy report 24 May 2022, adopted 7 July 2022; pages current through 2025/2026
supports: The strategy builds on a 2019 hydrodynamic stress test with Afvalwaterteam Etten and distinguishes short and prolonged rain, drought, heat and flood under KNMI 2050 context. It says all cores have roads/buildings exposed in the 70 mm/hour design exercise and that roads may become impassable for fire, police, ambulance and network operators.

For a primary-defence-failure scenario the strategy describes broad modeled inundation while parts of Wehl, Gaanderen, IJkenberg and the eastern rural area remain spared. This is planning/model evidence, not a selected current breach or T+72 forecast.

The municipality identifies Slingeland Hospital, fire/police headquarters, crisis centres/town hall/BUHA, pumps, locks, wastewater treatment, utility/telecom and transit stations as vital functions whose reachability matters.

The current crisis page at https://www.doetinchem.nl/veiligheid-en-crisis says Doetinchem has no emergency support points at present and aims to publish further information in Q4 2026. Its wildfire page at https://www.doetinchem.nl/natuurbrand-voorkomen provides preparedness advice. Neither page proves activation, capacity, access or restoration during an exercise.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Rijn en IJssel (WRIJ) / Nelen & Schuurmans
evidenceSources.title: Klimaatatlas Doetinchem, 2019 hydraulic stress test and flood-context services
evidenceSources.edition: Final technical report May 2019; ArcGIS item modified 9 October 2025
supports: The public StoryMap embeds 23 web maps. WRIJ's ArcGIS REST service https://opengeo.wrij.nl/arcgis/rest/services/Klimaat/KEA_DATA/MapServer exposes queryable short-rain water-depth layers for T100/T1000, short- and long-rain road passability, prolonged-rain depth, groundwater, warm-night, tree, heat-stress, groundwater-protection and affected-land-use layers.

The 2019 hydrodynamic model combines sewer, surface water, terrain and infiltration. Its scenarios include 70 mm/1 h, 90 mm/1 h, 160 mm/2 h and prolonged 120 mm/48 h rain; road classes are at most 10 cm passable, 10-30 cm emergency-only and at least 30 cm impassable.

The technical report explicitly describes theoretical events, average building-floor assumptions using AHN2 and uncertainty between modeled and real conditions. Those caveats prohibit treating the maps as current observations or precise outcomes.

The underlying Geodan WMS https://apps.geodan.nl/public/data/org/gws/YWFMLMWERURF/kea_public/wms exposes small-probability depth and 2050 place-based probability layers. Public ArcGIS/WMS access is integration-ready, but standard reuse licence, contractual cadence, source cell size and complete NoData semantics are not stated and must be cleared before causal ingestion.

WRIJ reports that a 340-metre Oude IJssel defence at Grutbroek/Keppelseweg was raised/strengthened and rainfall discharge improved by January 2025: https://www.wrij.nl/actueel/nieuwsoverzicht/dijkversterking-grutbroek-doetinchem-klaar. A completed upgrade is context, not proof of failure or guaranteed protection.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Rijn en IJssel / Het Waterschapshuis (HWH)
evidenceSources.title: Machine-readable water-control and wastewater registers for Doetinchem
evidenceSources.edition: Deployment snapshot 2 September 2026; WRIJ public FeatureServer current at access
supports: The generated municipality intersection contains 59 registered objects: five sewer pumps, RWZI Wehl, one surface-water pump and 52 weirs. Named pump capacities are present in the source but their units, operating envelopes and comparability are not established in the app.

HWH IMWA is a national weekly OGC API and HWH DAMO is a national contributor-dependent OGC API, both CC BY-SA 4.0. A registered or gerealiseerd object does not prove operation, connectivity, capacity, backup or restoration.

WRIJ also exposes a public query/extract FeatureServer at https://opengeo.wrij.nl/arcgis/rest/services/Leidingen/Zuiveringsbeheer/FeatureServer with pressure-sewer lines, appurtenances, RWZI, pumps and treatment areas. The service metadata does not state a standard reuse licence or fixed cadence; legal/security review is required before any topology is used causally.

The strongest safe current simulation role is official non-live context and completeness checking. Connected catchments, flow direction, control logic, compatible capacities, live pump/RWZI state, backup and repair remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025-2028
supports: VNOG evaluates flooding, nature fire, extreme weather and earthquake and separately assesses electricity, drinking-water, telecom and cyber disruption with domino effects across vital services.

The regional profile rates an extreme hot/dry summer very likely and very severe, extreme summer rain/wind likely and serious, and large nature fire likely and serious. It does not turn those regional judgements into Doetinchem neighbourhood probabilities or deterministic T+72 losses.

Damaging earthquake is not developed as a regional scenario because VNOG does not consider the area one where expected intensity causes personal/building damage. That supports only a low-screening interpretation, not an impossible-event claim.
This fixed expert planning PDF has no machine event API, explicit open-data licence or live refresh cadence. Its simulation role is hazard/lifeline mechanism and governance context only.

evidenceSources.title: Official forest, weather, seismic, rain-stress, water and agricultural context services
evidenceSources.edition: Risicokaart metadata updated 19 February 2026; current service/catalogue editions at access
supports: The Public Domain Risicokaart WFS type ISOR_RK:isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied returns a Doetinchem-owned mixed-forest polygon, feature isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied.0222060066961, valid since 31 March 2006. Point [6.364859124839539, 51.95926087155905] is inside that polygon, GM0222 and CBS neighbourhood BU02220408 Buitengebied - Slangenburg.

KNMI Data Platform/FDSN offers versioned weather/radar and earthquake-event services; named radar products are typically five-minute observations and default KNMI open products use CC BY 4.0. No earthquake origin matched GM0222 in the audit snapshot; catalogue absence is not zero probability.

The national Klimaateffectatlas/Rijkswaterstaat 70 mm/2 h WMS is a CC0 static scenario layer with catalogue metadata updated 5 August 2026. It is official context, not current rain, an incident footprint or a substitute for Doetinchem's finer stress test.

RVO's definitive 2025 BRP crop-parcel service is annual and accessible via PDOK WMS/WFS/Atom under the current CC0 metadata. Parcels are land-use context, not current fuel moisture, crop condition, yield, food stock or service availability.

Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo generally publishes ten-minute point observations under CC0 and is non-mission-critical. Zero stations assigned inside GM0222 is no point coverage, never zero water level/discharge or safety.

evidenceSources.publisher: Liander / Netbeheer Nederland / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / RIVM / Slingeland Ziekenhuis / DUO / RDI / NDW
evidenceSources.title: Machine-readable power, provider, care, education, antenna and traffic public context
evidenceSources.edition: Public snapshots inspected 2 September 2026; RIVM acute-care questionnaire 2026 v1.1
supports: Liander's CC BY 4.0 ArcGIS service returns OS LANGERAK 150/10 kV and OS DOETINCHEM 150/20/10 kV in the Doetinchem bbox. Item/edit timestamps exist but no contractual geometry cadence, current load, switching, exposure, backup or restoration is published.

One public DUO-postcode sample for Netbeheer Nederland identifies a Liander service area and planning queues/capacity; publisher updates capacity/projects at least quarterly and queues monthly. It is one planning sample, not municipal coverage, physical topology, outage or T+72 state; the publisher calls it open data but the exact licence and stable public endpoint are unstated.

The Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting WMS/WFS at https://public.geodata.mijnaansluiting.nl/geoserver/mijnaansluiting_open/ows supplies provider-responsibility polygons with provider timestamps. They do not show pipes, cables, connectivity, coverage quality, state or capacity.

The CC0 RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1, published 3 July 2026, records Slingeland Ziekenhuis at Kruisbergseweg 25 as 24/7 emergency and acute-obstetric care with twelve treatment rooms and 17,000 reported 2025 visits. Slingeland's current page confirms 24/7 ED context: https://www.slingeland.nl/locatie-spoedeisende-hulp. Neither source is live occupancy, staffing, access, diversion, generator or fuel state.

The generated public context has 61 DUO education locations (national daily refresh around 06:15 under attribution terms), 106 RDI antenna sites representing 225 antennas (live statutory WFS, reuse licence/cadence unstated), seven coarse KVK/PDOK government-service points, and zero current NDW situations or RIVM PM2.5 stations. Schools and offices are not shelters; antennas are not coverage/backhaul; every zero is a time/coverage result, not open/clean/safe state.

identity.summary: GM0222, Doetinchem, Gelderland and safety region Noord- en Oost-Gelderland are internally and officially coherent.
notes: Generated feature id, municipality bundle code/name, province and exactly one safety-region assignment agree.
The context gate verifies centre [6.280163177126242, 51.965125985136545] lies inside the generated overview.
Boundary/statistics edition 2025, older stress-test model editions, current public observations and synthetic scenario time remain distinct.

geography.summary: The one-component generalized outline is topologically coherent but too coarse for flood, sewer, road, forest or facility intersection.
notes: Fresh official geometry has one component/one ring/4,110 positions; the overview preserves component/ring count with 174 positions.
Use full-resolution annual CBS geometry and explicit land/water/coverage masks for analysis; retain the compact outline for overview rendering and selection only.
Representative neighbourhood points do not represent the full geometry of inundation, urban heat, vegetation, roads, residents or assets.

demography.summary: Official municipal controls and neighbourhood population reconcile within CBS publication rounding semantics.
notes: CBS reports 60,049 residents; 84 neighbourhood source rows sum to 60,050 (+1, +0.002%).
CBS reports 13,688 residents aged 65+ and 9,860 one-person households; neighbourhood age-65+ rows sum to 13,650.
Largest source rows include Oosseld/Vijverberg-zuid 2,820, De IJkenberg 2,500, 't Hagelkruis 2,395, Overstegen-west 2,245 and Het Hartger/De Elshof-noord 2,210.
Registered residents are allocation denominators, not timestamped presence, evacuation demand, care need, visitor counts or individual vulnerability.

regionalDetail.summary: Eighty-four neighbourhoods give granular census context, but missing indicators and public registers cannot supply hazard exposure or live service state.
notes: District-heating and charging fields are missing for all 84 rows; property value is present for ten, car ownership for 22, several housing/benefit fields for 76 and doctor/supermarket/density fields for 81.
Null and suppressed remain Unknown, never zero. Source coverage, observation/effective time, unit, quality and simulation role must survive ingestion and export.

The 59 water objects, 61 education locations, 106 antenna sites, seven government points, one hospital and two high-voltage stations are non-live context and do not establish connectivity, occupancy, state or restoration.

settlements.summary: BAG and BRT references retain Doetinchem, Gaanderen, Wehl and rural labels without changing municipal identity.
notes: BAG has three woonplaatsen: Doetinchem, Gaanderen and Wehl.
BRT adds nine descriptive settlement labels, yielding twelve generated labels across five buurtschappen, one deelkern and six woonkernen.
Settlements are cartographic context, not incident-time population, isolation, service continuity or hazard footprint.

transport.summary: Road, rail and transit references are present, but the causal graph is ten border-road proxies duplicated across every service.
notes: Ten A18/N-road links cover three neighbouring municipalities with nominal scenario-unit capacities 260/150; they are not measured throughput, emergency access or future passability.
Four ProRail stations and 77 GTFS stop areas are static reference/schedule context, not rail, bus, ambulance, evacuation or repair continuity.
The local rain stress test explicitly provides emergency-road passability classes, but the simulation does not sample them.
All eight services expose the identical road IDs. NWB cannot substantiate electricity, drinking-water, drainage, gas, telecom or facility transfer.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong local planning and public facility/water context exists, but it is not an incident-valid response or recovery state.
notes: Municipal and VNOG evidence covers rain/flood, heat/drought, nature fire, wind/winter, earthquake screening, cyber and lifeline cascades.
Doetinchem currently reports no emergency support points; candidate public offices or schools cannot be promoted to command, reception, shelter or distribution roles without confirmation.
Slingeland's 24/7 registration is valuable care context, not incident-time accessibility, acceptance, occupancy, staffing or backup.
Current/no-match NDW, Waterinfo, air-quality, power or seismic data must retain retrieval and valid time and cannot be projected into synthetic T+72.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0222 pnpm audit:model passed one file/two tests in 32.55 seconds (32.35 seconds test time) for severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services.
The canonical apps/web/src/scenarios.ts factory delegates to the sim-core presets, preventing web/core preset drift.

A focused reproduction with an official forest-contained fire source passed one test in 33.07 seconds (32.98 seconds import; 1 ms test) and recorded scenario, spatial, network, ledger and recovery values.

A headless Chromium run at 1440x900 selected Doetinchem, river flood, Drinking water and T+24/T+72 without console errors or horizontal overflow. The inspector labeled the result 'Official context + scenario', the network a logical corridor proxy, and zero local Waterinfo observations as no data rather than zero/safe.

numericalInvariants.summary: Outputs are finite, bounded, deterministic, exact at zero input and locally reconciled.
notes: Exact-zero intensity gives zero maximum severity, affected population-equivalent and attributable person-hours for every preset.
Compound T+24 has 84 rows summing to population 60,049 and affected 31,521; maximum all-service reconciliation error is 1.4210854715202004e-14.
Changing the selected service layer does not mutate municipality hazard, pressure or affected values.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One source-insensitive neighbourhood seed creates precise local rankings across unrelated hazards and ignores a controlled forest source.
notes: Pluvial, river, coastal, heat and wildfire have the exact same complete 84-neighbourhood order: De Huet - fase 1 + 3, Buitengebied - Pinnedijk, Nieuw Wehl - centrum, Wehl - noordoost and Verheulsweide - zuid lead each.
WRIJ and Doetinchem publish distinct short/long-rain depth, road-passability, groundwater, flood and heat mechanisms; none determines the rank.

With source [6.364859124839539, 51.95926087155905] inside the official mixed-forest polygon and BU02220408 Buitengebied - Slangenburg, direct municipal fire peaks 0.397064 at T+11, but the source neighbourhood ranks 28/84 while De Huet leads.
The compound output declares no unsupported hazard families even though none of the nine local hazard families has a Doetinchem calibration contract.

serviceDependencies.summary: Every lifeline copies the same ten road links despite sector-specific public context and absent physical network evidence.
notes: A18/N-road IDs and scenario capacities are identical for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
NWB supports road geometry; it does not establish Liander/Vitens/gas/telecom feeders, sewer or surface-water flow, hospital dependency, stocks or response logistics.

Public substations, provider polygons, water objects, antennas, education/government/care points and rail/transit references are context only and provide no compatible service capacity, customer mapping, backup or restoration.
Unavailable or security-sensitive topology must remain Unknown. A transparent non-spatial synthetic service index is the smallest acceptable fallback.

causalTrace.summary: Municipality, hazard, service-dependency and route ledgers close, while attribution is correctly identified as modeled rather than empirical.
notes: Focused checks verify deterministic counterfactuals, dimension shares, service-pressure contributions and local/network identities for all scenario/service/checkpoint combinations.
The trace states that system-pressure weights are model assumptions and event-attributable burden excludes intermunicipal transfers.
Logical route-flow arithmetic closes, but arithmetic traceability does not make road-shaped utility transfer physically causal.
Exact burden is an availability proxy, not observed customer-outage hours, health outcome, displacement or economic loss.

recovery72h.summary: Standing-water repair guards behave internally, but local first-72-hour response and restoration timing is unvalidated.
notes: River T+72 retains severity 0.627563, normalized inundation stress 2.000988, 28,725 affected, 2,128,326.509 cumulative person-hours, supply availability 0.152470 and zero recovery across all eight services.
Compound T+72 retains flood stress 0.436401 and cyber severity 0.054274, 34,211 affected, 2,100,622.833 person-hours, supply availability 0.154161 and zero recovery across all services.

Storm, pluvial, winter and wildfire forcing clear by T+72; heat remains active while affected rounds to zero; cyber decays. These are deterministic exercise mechanics rather than Doetinchem/operator restoration promises.
No selected defence, sewer/pump, utility, road/rail, hospital, support-point, crew, backup, stock, dewatering or repair state supports precise T+24/T+72 availability.

findings.summary: Generated identity, safety-region membership, population control, neighbourhoods and settlements are coherent.
findings.evidence: CBS gives 60,049 residents; 84 neighbourhood rows sum to 60,050 (+0.002%) and reconcile without rewriting published values. Code, name, province, safety region, BAG places and BRT labels agree; the full and overview geometries retain one component/ring.
findings.action: Retain official editions, full-versus-overview geometry purpose, CBS rounding/suppression, source-versus-allocated totals and null semantics on every refresh.

findings.summary: The named-major-river screen produces severe persistent Doetinchem inundation without a selected hydraulic event or defence state.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 severity is 0.627563 and internal normalized inundation stress 2.000988; T+72 reports 28,725 affected, 2,128,326.509 attributable person-hours, 15.247% supply availability and zero recovery for every service. No Oude IJssel/IJssel boundary hydrograph, gauge/datum, Grutbroek or other defence state, breach/overtopping, connected footprint, arrival, recession or dewatering path is selected. The municipality's broad defence-failure map and completed Grutbroek upgrade are contextual scenarios, not event evidence.
findings.action: Require a WRIJ/WMCN-approved named, versioned hydraulic event with source, level/datum, defence state, connected footprint, arrival/recession, uncertainty and NoData before direct exposure is releasable. Otherwise show Unknown and retain the scalar only as a non-operational diagnostic.

findings.summary: A single neighbourhood order is reused across physically unrelated hazards.
findings.evidence: Pluvial, river, coastal, heat and wildfire share the exact full 84-row order led by De Huet - fase 1 + 3, Buitengebied - Pinnedijk and Nieuw Wehl - centrum. WRIJ's hazard-specific rain, road, groundwater, heat and flood layers and the official forest geometry do not drive local allocation; compound incorrectly reports unsupported=[] despite absent local calibration.
findings.action: Mark all nine GM0222 hazard families unsupported and suppress hotspot precision until mechanism-specific versioned surfaces have unit, resolution, coverage, NoData, edition/effective time, licence, uncertainty and declared simulation role.

findings.summary: The model ignores Doetinchem's machine-readable hydrodynamic rainfall and emergency-road evidence.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports severity 0.305280, flood stress 0.422695, 6,302 affected and 245,802.221 person-hours, then zero forcing/affected at T+72 and 553,618.389 cumulative person-hours. The 2019 local model supplies separate 70 mm/1 h, 90 mm/1 h, 160 mm/2 h and 120 mm/48 h depth/passability outputs using sewer, surface-water, terrain and infiltration inputs; the simulator samples none of them and offers no local duration/dewatering calibration.
findings.action: Integrate governed WRIJ ArcGIS/WMS surfaces as official scenario context first, pin theoretical event, model edition, unit, cell size, road-depth class, NoData, coverage, uncertainty, licence and affectsSimulation; enable causal use only after authorization and validation against the full boundary.

findings.summary: Direct wildfire allocation does not follow a controlled source inside Slangenburg forest.
findings.evidence: The canonical wildfire is locally smoke-only and peaks T+11 at severity 0.147916/smoke 0.377650. In a focused test, an ignition inside official Risicokaart mixed forest and BU02220408 Buitengebied - Slangenburg creates direct municipal fire 0.397064 at T+11, yet the containing neighbourhood ranks 28/84 and De Huet - fase 1 + 3 remains first.
findings.action: Require official eligible vegetation plus named ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, valid-time wind, access and suppression-water inputs for direct flame. Enforce source/perimeter-responsive allocation and keep remote smoke as a separate mechanism; absent ignition/perimeter is Unknown.

findings.summary: Water and drainage impacts ignore a substantial but incomplete public managed-water/wastewater context.
findings.evidence: The boundary intersects 59 HWH records—five sewer pumps, RWZI Wehl, one surface-water pump and 52 weirs—and WRIJ exposes pressure lines, pumps, treatment and areas through a FeatureServer. The model has no catchment, connectivity, flow direction, compatible capacity units, current state, control logic, backup or repair link. A source capacity or 'gerealiseerd' label cannot be converted into live performance.
findings.action: Ingest HWH objects and an authorized WRIJ extract as non-live typed context, separate potable water, wastewater and surface-water control, and obtain only safe aggregate catchment/dependency/state bands. Where topology or operating data is unavailable/security-sensitive, show Unknown rather than inferred road transfer.

findings.summary: The same ten NWB roads are presented as transfer paths for all eight essential services.
findings.evidence: Power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply all reuse A18/N315/N316/N317/N813/N814/N815 links and 260/150 scenario-unit capacities. NWB establishes roads only. Liander stations, provider polygons, HWH objects, RDI antennas, four rail stations, 77 stops, Slingeland and public offices/schools do not establish physical service connectivity, compatible capacity, current availability, backup or restoration.
findings.action: Restrict NWB/NDW/rail/transit to mobility and separately evidenced supply/repair access. Require sector-specific safe aggregate interfaces for utilities and facilities; otherwise expose transparent non-spatial synthetic indices with no operator attribution.

findings.summary: Precise first-72-hour service and recovery output lacks a confirmed local action/resource ledger.
findings.evidence: Doetinchem currently says it has no emergency support points. Slingeland's static 24/7 role, seven government records and 61 education sites do not prove incident-time access, staffing, capacity, shelter/distribution status or backup. River and compound hold all recovery at zero through T+72, while other scenarios recover on exact trajectories, but no municipality, VNOG, water-board or operator action/state substantiates those paths.
findings.action: Add a proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled action ledger with owner, source, issue/valid time, expiry, geography, dependency, resource/capacity and confidence. Treat support points, hospital acceptance, crews, backup, stocks and restoration as Unknown until authority/operator confirmation.

findings.summary: Wind, coastal, heat/drought, winter, cyber, earthquake and compound values are bounded exercises rather than local observations or forecasts.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 has zero direct water and 0 affected, a plausible narrow inland screen, but nonzero wind/indirect burden is generic. VNOG supports severe weather, hot/dry summer, cyber/lifeline cascade and low damaging-earthquake relevance; the model selects no named weather replay/forecast, cyber target/architecture or seismic event/ground-motion grid. Earthquake peaks between checkpoints at 0.032459 severity/0.010387 g and zero affected; heat remains severity 0.101267/drought 0.562594 at T+72 while affected rounds to zero. Compound inherits unsupported spatial and infrastructure assumptions.
findings.action: Retain explicit synthetic/derived/indirect/scoped labels and sensitivity. Use KNMI observations/forecasts only with dataset/version, issue/valid time and lead; require named cyber and earthquake events/targets before direct local consequences, and never infer safety from absence of an event or station.

findings.summary: Null, no-match, true-zero and modeled-zero states need an enforced shared semantic contract.
findings.evidence: GM0222 has zero locally assigned Waterinfo stations, PM2.5 stations and current NDW situations; these mean no intersecting point/message at retrieval, not zero water, smoke or disruption. Missing CBS district heat/charging and partial housing/mobility fields are Unknown. Coastal direct water and exact zero-intensity output are genuine scoped/model zeros. Browser text explains Waterinfo NoData, but hazard rankings and compound unsupported=[] still imply unsupported precision.
findings.action: Across maps, legends, APIs and exports distinguish observed/modeled value including zero, Unknown/not covered and not applicable; preserve publisher, licence, coverage, edition, retrieval/issue/valid time, unit, quality, uncertainty and affectsSimulation.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic, reconciliation, causal-ledger and sustained-water contract passes for GM0222.
findings.evidence: The focused gates cover ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite/bounded/deterministic, zero intensity is exact, 60,049 residents and all 84 neighbourhoods reconcile, ledgers close, attributable burden is monotone, selected layer is invariant and standing water blocks repair. Browser inspection exposes logical-route and no-data caveats.
findings.action: Keep GM0222 and national ALL coverage in regression and add assertions for hazard-specific ranks, source containment, hydraulic event contracts, local rain coverage, route separation, action state and explicit unsupported/NoData rendering.

corrections.summary: Replace GM0222's generic major-river screen with an explicit Oude IJssel/IJssel hydraulic and defence-state contract or an honest Unknown result.
corrections.validation: Best machine-readable inputs are WRIJ's official climate/flood ArcGIS REST/WMS (Doetinchem/Etten-area static modeled coverage; technical edition May 2019, ArcGIS item modified October 2025; public access but standard licence, contractual cadence, cell size and complete NoData not stated), WRIJ legal/water services, HWH IMWA weekly and DAMO contributor-variable OGC APIs (national, CC BY-SA 4.0), RWS Waterinfo points (national, generally ten-minute, CC0, non-mission-critical) and an expert-selected LIWO/WMCN flood scenario (national OGC/download; layer edition/licence must be checked). Intersect the 4,110-position official boundary. Require named source and version, gauge/level/datum, boundary hydrograph, defence segment/state, breach/overtopping assumption, connected footprint, arrival/recession/dewatering, resolution/unit, coverage/NoData, uncertainty, valid time, licence and authority approval; otherwise direct exposure is Unknown and scalar amplitude remains diagnostic only.

corrections.summary: Replace the common 84-neighbourhood seed with governed hazard-specific rain, heat, groundwater and flood surfaces.

corrections.summary: Add a valid-time evidence/action contract for first-72-hour care, support, observations and recovery without converting registers into operations.
corrections.validation: RIVM acute-care v1.1 is a national CC0 fixed 3 July 2026 questionnaire; DUO RIO is national/daily around 06:15 under attribution terms; KVK/PDOK government-service points are national Public Domain registration context; RDI is a national live statutory WFS with licence/cadence unstated; Waterinfo is generally ten-minute/CC0; NDW DATEX II is valid-time traffic context; NBNL is quarterly/monthly planning context with exact licence/stable endpoint unstated. Store source, coverage/resolution, edition, observation/issue/valid/retrieval time, cadence, licence, quality, NoData and affectsSimulation. Add proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled action state and owner/resource/expiry/confidence; no support point, hospital, school, office, antenna or zero-match observation becomes operational availability or a T+72 forecast without confirmation.

residualLimitations: This is an audit of a deterministic first-72-hour planning exercise, not a warning, probability estimate, hydraulic assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, clinical-capacity statement or operator restoration commitment.

No expert-selected Oude IJssel/IJssel hydrograph, gauge/datum, defence state, breach/overtopping path, connected footprint, arrival/recession, dewatering, verified depth unit or NoData mask is ingested; normalized inundation stress is not metres.

Doetinchem/WRIJ's 2019 stress test is official static modeled scenario evidence with documented theoretical/height limitations, not current or forecast conditions; causal reuse needs licence, resolution, NoData and authority clearance.

The generalized 174-position CBS outline is appropriate for overview rendering, not detailed water, defence, sewer, road, forest, building or asset intersections; use the full 4,110-position geometry.
CBS neighbourhood values can be rounded or suppressed; the +1 source sum difference is publication semantics, null fields remain Unknown, and registered residents do not equal incident-time presence.
HWH and WRIJ registers do not establish complete connected catchments, compatible capacity units, current pump/weir/RWZI state, control logic, backup, contamination, pressure or restoration.

No complete public causal Liander feeder/switching, Vitens pipe/pressure/quality, gas pressure-district, municipal sewer, telecom backhaul or facility/service topology is consumed; unavailable or security-sensitive detail remains Unknown.
NWB roads, NDW messages, ProRail stations and GTFS stops do not establish incident-time road/rail/bus operation, evacuation throughput, bridge/crossing state, emergency access or repair access.
Slingeland's registered 24/7 role and questionnaire counts do not establish travel time, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, diversion, generator/fuel or backup endurance.

Government and education locations are not confirmed crisis centres, emergency support points, shelters, care sites or distribution points; Doetinchem currently states that no emergency support points exist.
RDI antenna records do not establish operator, coverage, backhaul, traffic, power/backup, damage, congestion, availability or restoration; provider polygons identify responsibility context only.
Zero Waterinfo, PM2.5 and current NDW matches and absence of a KNMI earthquake origin are source/time/coverage outcomes, not zero water, smoke, road disruption, ground motion or risk.
Wildfire lacks a canonical local ignition/perimeter, current fuel/moisture, wind, access, suppression-water and response model; the Slangenburg point is a reproducible diagnostic, not a forecast.

Cyber lacks a named target, architecture, attack path, detection and containment state; earthquake lacks a selected event, site-response field and fragility; generic weather lacks a versioned issue/valid-time forecast or replay.

Coastal direct zero applies only to the current inland direct-water screen and does not mean no wind, supply-chain or cross-boundary consequence; river wording does not by itself select an Oude IJssel mechanism.

Household preparedness, mutual aid, emergency-water/support points, crews, stocks, backup and recovery are scenario assumptions unless confirmed in an incident/action ledger; 72 hours is a planning horizon, not a restoration deadline.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not observed customer outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss; six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid transitions and T+72 excludes prolonged recovery.
